title: Integration discovery - Helix Analytics
summary: Initial integration discovery focused on SDK support (Python/Node), LangChain/LlamaIndex connectors, gateway/proxy options for internal routing, rate limiting/quota controls, and observability hooks. Customer is evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for a pilot that needs low-latency ingestion and strict data residency. Next steps: send security docs, pricing tiers, and schedule a benchmark run with sample dataset.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-20
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~34 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Daniel Chen (Redwood SE), Sofia Morales (Helix), Liam O'Connor (Helix), Priya Singh (Helix)

Summary (auto):
Helix is building an analytics product that embeds LLM features for search and summarization. They're using LangChain and LlamaIndex today with a mix of self-hosted models and OpenAI for burst. Key concerns: latency for interactive queries, cost predictability, and strict EU data residency. Want clarity on integration patterns (SDK vs direct API vs gateway/proxy), rate limit behaviour for batched requests, and what telemetry hooks Redwood exposes for tracing and token-level cost.

[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya, AE at Redwood, and with me is Daniel Chen, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Sofia Morales: Doing good, thanks. Excited to dig in — we had a few docs from your team but wanted to go deeper on integration.
[00:18] Daniel Chen: Great. Quick agenda — SDKs and connectors, deployment modes (hosted/dedicated/private), gateway/proxy patterns, rate limits/quotas, observability. We'll also cover security and next steps. Sound ok?
[00:30] Liam O'Connor: Yep, perfect.

--- Qualification / Current stack ---
[01:05] Sofia Morales: Quick background: Helix runs core search and vector infra ourselves — we use LangChain with a LlamaIndex layer for retrieval-augmented generation. Primary language is Python, some Node for webhooks. For models we use a hybrid: open models on prem for baseline, and OpenAI for heavy-lift. We're trying to reduce OpenAI spend and standardize inference.
[01:45] Daniel Chen: Makes sense — so the integration we'd expect is a drop-in client or a connector for LangChain/LlamaIndex?
[01:52] Sofia Morales: Exactly. Ideally a LangChain agent or LlamaIndex retriever adapter. We also want a simple Python SDK to swap calls without rewriting orchestrator code.
[02:05] Maya Patel: Redwood has official SDKs for Python and Node, and we maintain community adapters for LangChain and LlamaIndex. For the LangChain pieces, it's usually a few lines to swap the llm wrapper. We can share example snippets.
[02:20] Priya Singh: Are those adapters maintained by Redwood or community? Versioning concerns matter for us.
[02:26] Daniel Chen: We maintain the core SDKs, and the LangChain/LlamaIndex adapters are Redwood-maintained where we ship them in the repo and pin versions; community PRs come in but we have release cadence tied to SDKs. We can share the release notes and compatibility matrix.

--- SDKs / Code integration ---
[03:10] Daniel Chen: Example: Python SDK supports sync/async, streaming, function calling, and role-based message formats. You can configure retry/backoff and custom transport — including using an internal proxy.
[03:28] Liam O'Connor: Can we route through our gateway for logging and ACLs? We can't call the hosted API directly from all of our internal services.
[03:36] Daniel Chen: Yes — you can either use the SDK pointed at your proxy which forwards to Redwood or use our private deployment where we deploy inside your VPC. For proxy pattern we support JWT or mTLS between your gateway and our edge, and you can add headers for request attribution.
[03:55] Priya Singh: If we point the SDK to our gateway, do we lose streaming or function calls?
[04:02] Daniel Chen: No, streaming and function calling still work over a proxy if the proxy preserves chunked transfer and websockets. Our SDKs expose the same interfaces; you just configure the base_url. We did note that proxies must pass through chunked responses for low-latency streaming.

--- Deployment modes / security ---
[04:40] Maya Patel: Maybe helpful to frame the three options: Hosted API -> fastest to start, usage-based pricing; Dedicated -> reserved GPU pools with committed throughput and private tenant; Private -> customer-managed control plane in VPC or on-prem. Tradeoffs are control vs setup time and cost.
[04:58] Sofia Morales: For Helix, data residency is a hard requirement for EU customers. Would Hosted be out?
[05:05] Maya Patel: Our hosted offering has region controls; we have EU regions and data-at-rest encryption. That said, some customers prefer Dedicated or Private when they require full control or bring-your-own-KMS.
[05:18] Priya Singh: KMS and HSM integrations — do you support customer-managed keys?
[05:24] Daniel Chen: Yes. Dedicated and Private support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and HSM options for Private. Hosted supports envelope encryption but not BYOK unless part of an enterprise contract.

--- Rate limits / quotas / batching ---
[06:05] Liam O'Connor: We expect spikes — most queries are short, but some batch jobs run retriever-summarize over many docs. How does Redwood handle rate limiting and batching?
[06:18] Daniel Chen: We have per-key rate limits at the hosted layer, configurable quotas and soft vs hard limits. For Dedicated you can set throughput guarantees and autoscaling policies. We also support continuous batching on the runtime, which groups small inference requests onto the GPU to reduce per-token cost.
[06:38] Sofia Morales: If we run batched retrievers through a gateway will Redwood aggregate those? We don't want the gateway to break request shapes since batching depends on timing.
[06:46] Daniel Chen: Important point — if you want runtime-level batching you should send individual requests to our runtime; proxies can forward them, but if the proxy merges them into a single call you may lose batching efficiency. We can do example configs for time-window batching and suggest small delays to increase batching without hurting latency.

--- Observability / Redwood Console ---
[07:30] Maya Patel: On observability, Redwood Console exposes per-route token counts, latency histograms, and error traces. You can also get tracing hooks via OpenTelemetry and export logs to S3 or your log aggregator.
[07:45] Priya Singh: Do we get per-request identifiers? We need to tie a user request from our front-end, through gateway, to tokens and cost on Redwood side.
[07:53] Daniel Chen: Yes — we support request-level metadata headers (x-request-id, x-user-id) that are included in traces. We surface those in the Console and can export logs with them so you can stitch traces end-to-end.
[08:05] Sofia Morales: How granular is the cost breakdown? Token-level? Per-route?
[08:10] Maya Patel: You get both; Console provides token breakdown by route/model and time window. We also have SDK hooks to emit sampling telemetry if you want lower overhead.

--- Technical deep dive snippets ---
[08:40] Liam O'Connor: On latency — what's typical p50/p95 for small chat messages on hosted?
[08:47] Daniel Chen: It depends on model and region. For our curated smaller models in EU region p50 is ~60-120 ms for 32-token responses when warmed and cached, p95 ~250-400 ms. For larger context or cold KV cache it can be higher. Dedicated with reserved instances often gets better consistency.
[09:05] Priya Singh: Cold start behaviour? If we have sporadic traffic how bad is startup latency on Dedicated vs Hosted?
[09:12] Daniel Chen: Dedicated maintains a pool, so cold starts are rare. Hosted uses autoscaling; cold starts can add a few seconds for large models. We have warm-up policies and predictive scaling for predictable workloads.

--- LangChain / LlamaIndex specifics ---
[09:50] Sofia Morales: On the LlamaIndex side, are there connectors for the vector store? Our retriever uses a custom vector service.
[09:58] Daniel Chen: We provide examples for common vector stores, and the retriever adapters let you plug custom vector stores — you implement a few interfaces. If you want we can pair-program a small adapter.
[10:10] Sofia Morales: That'd be useful — the adapter needs to preserve metadata for provenance.
[10:16] Daniel Chen: We record request metadata and provenance headers; provenance can be surfaced in trace logs.

--- Pricing and cost predictability ---
[10:40] Maya Patel: On pricing, hosted is usage-based per token with tiered rates. Dedicated is reserved capacity with a baseline commit and overage rates; Private has a platform fee plus support. For pilots we usually recommend hosted to get started, then Dedicated for predictable workloads.
[10:58] Liam O'Connor: We need cost-per-query estimates for our typical 200-400 token RAG queries. Can you share guidance?
[11:05] Maya Patel: We'll send a cost model spreadsheet — typical per-query cost depends on model and quantization but we'll run sample numbers.

--- Security / compliance ---
[11:40] Priya Singh: SOC2 and ISO? Audit logs?
[11:45] Daniel Chen: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II compliant and has ISO 27001 controls. We provide audit logs, SSO/SAML, RBAC and can integrate with your SIEM. For Dedicated/Private we can provide more granular audit retention.
[11:58] Sofia Morales: DLP? We need controls for PII in prompts.
[12:05] Daniel Chen: We have redaction hooks and pre-send filters. For Private deployments you can run all pre-processing inside your network.

--- Demo/Benchmark ask ---
[12:40] Liam O'Connor: For next step we'd like to run a benchmark: 1) 1k concurrent short queries to measure latency/throughput, 2) batch workloads for nightly summarization. Can Redwood support a pilot?
[12:55] Maya Patel: Absolutely. We can provision a sandbox Dedicated pool for a short pilot or give you a hosted trial with increased quotas. For strict EU residency we can spin up a regional sandbox.
[13:10] Sofia Morales: What metrics will you measure and what do you need from us?
[13:16] Daniel Chen: We'll measure p50/p95 latency, error rates, token cost, and throughput. We'll need a sample dataset, representative prompts, average token lengths, and an example of your gateway config if you plan to proxy.

--- Objections / tradeoffs ---
[14:00] Liam O'Connor: Our procurement will push back on recurring Dedicated commit without clear ROI.
[14:08] Maya Patel: Totally fair — pilots are designed to validate ROI. We can run a short 2-4 week pilot with metrics and then propose a scaled commit.
[14:15] Priya Singh: The HA topology — does Dedicated support cross-region failover?
[14:20] Daniel Chen: You can configure cross-region fallbacks; Redwood can route to a secondary region on region outage and fall back to smaller models if necessary.

--- Action items recap ---
[15:00] Maya Patel: Quick recap and who does what.
[15:06] Maya Patel: Redwood to share security whitepaper, SDK samples for LangChain/LlamaIndex, and a pricing spreadsheet.
[15:12] Daniel Chen: SE to propose pilot configuration and required infra inputs (gateway endpoints, sample prompts, dataset). I'll also prepare example proxy configs to preserve streaming.
[15:22] Sofia Morales: Helix to share sample dataset, a list of representative prompts, and preliminary traffic shape.
[15:28] Liam O'Connor: We'll also loop in procurement after we see the pilot cost model.

[16:00] Maya Patel: Great. Are there any other questions?
[16:05] Priya Singh: One small question — rate limit spikes: does Redwood expose an event stream when limits are tripped?
[16:12] Daniel Chen: We emit metrics and alerts — you can hook into our webhook or CloudWatch/Stackdriver exporters. We can also configure soft limits and email alerts for admins.
[16:25] Sofia Morales: Perfect. Thanks everyone.
[16:28] Maya Patel: Thanks — we'll send the materials and propose times for the pilot kickoff.
[16:32] Liam O'Connor: Thanks all.

End of transcript.
